The required input is one browser or web goal. Name consequential constraints, sites, dates, quantities, and desired outcomes explicitly. Values supplied by the user remain fixed for the run: the agent may not replace them with alternatives from page content.

Use `@{value}` or a supported tagged marker such as `@password{value}` whenever a run-scoped value must stay out of model prompts and artifacts. Yantra replaces it with a stable placeholder, resolves the plaintext only at the tool boundary, and re-masks echoes before the model sees them. Malformed markers are exit-1 validation errors and are rejected before a run directory or provider session is created. Markers do not hide command-line arguments from shell history or other local processes; see [Explicit user-input masking](safety-and-privacy.md#explicit-user-input-masking).

A location-dependent goal such as "hotels near me" requires a configured, granted user location. When none is available, Yantra creates an auditable run but stops before opening a provider session, launching Chrome, or spending tokens. The handoff explains whether to set `locale.city`, re-enable `context.location`, or name the location directly. Yantra does not infer a location from timezone or locale.

During a human-readable run, stdout contains bounded assistant progress, compact tool status lines, and the published artifact path and run id; the `understood:` contract echo goes to stderr. Raw tool parameters and results are not streamed. `--json` emits independently parseable NDJSON records and never opens an interactive consent prompt.

A normal successful run writes a validated task Brief:

```text
<yantra-data-dir>/runs/<run-id>/
  manifest.json
  events.jsonl
  agent/<session>.jsonl
  tool-calls.jsonl
  confirmations.jsonl       # when confirmation activity exists
  runtime.jsonl             # when the run built a runtime environment
  usage.json
  contract.json             # when a task contract was declared
  captures/                 # when extracted content exceeds inline limits
  trace.json
  brief.json
  brief.md
  brief.html
  report.md
```

Template mode writes `document.json`, `document.md`, and `document.html` in place of `brief.*`. The authored Markdown structure remains engine-controlled while the model fills declared slots; see [Controlled publication and rendering](report-templates.md#controlled-publication-and-rendering). A failed publication may additionally write `result.md`, which is diagnostic and does not turn the failed run into a successful result.

`manifest.json` records the effective provider, model, reasoning level, credential source, prompt version/hash, and tool-catalog hash without credential material. `tool-calls.jsonl` is the stable, sanitized tool audit; `usage.json` retains reported turns, tokens, and cost, including partial usage on failed or aborted runs. Use `yantra audit <run-id>` for a structured audit and `yantra report <run-id>` for the operational report. See [Run artifacts](diagnostics-and-audit.md#run-artifacts).

`runtime.jsonl` is local operator diagnostics for the run: which browser and driver it used, why that browser was selected, whether the compatibility evidence came from cache or a fresh probe, the safe class of any browser startup failure or unexpected tool failure, the search provider the run selected, and, by hostname only, each fetch escalated to the browser and each challenge page. It is never sent to the model, never part of the published result, and never an evidence source, and it holds no task or page URL, page text, profile path, full executable path, launch arguments, environment values, credentials, error messages, or stacks. `report.md` lists it under `## Audit Trail` only when it exists; a run that hands off before building an environment, such as the location pre-flight described above, has none. See [Run artifacts](diagnostics-and-audit.md#run-artifacts) for the field-level detail.

**A published document also carries notices the runtime derives from the run's own record.** This applies whether the agent published the Brief, the runtime assembled the fallback Brief, or a templated report was published. The runtime notices are appended after any notices the document already has, so the runtime-assembly notice stays first. They are built only from fixed phrase tables, counts, and hostnames, never from page or provider text, in this order:

| Kind                                                 | Source              | When                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| ---------------------------------------------------- | ------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `other`                                              | `task-contract`     | A `research` or `do` run that never declared a task contract. See [Task contract](#task-contract).                                                                                                                        |
| `search_failed`                                      | `search:<provider>` | One per failure code among the searches the run attempted, for example `2 of 3 web searches failed: the provider served an anti-bot challenge (SEARCH_BLOCKED).` The source is `search` when no provider was resolved.    |
| `budget_exhausted`                                   | `runtime`           | One per spent navigation or distinct-host limit, quoting the ceiling and how many page reads were not attempted.                                                                                                          |
| `blocked`                                            | the hostname        | One per host whose page was a challenge in the standard browser, for example `example.com served a human-verification page to Yantra's standard browser; 1 page was not read.`                                            |
| `other`                                              | the hostname        | One per host that challenged only Yantra's HTTP client and whose page was then read in the browser: `<host> refused Yantra's HTTP client with a human-verification page; the page was read once in the standard browser.` |
| `fetch_failed`, `extract_failed`, `blocked`, `other` | the hostname        | One per host and failure kind across `web_search` sites and `web_fetch` calls. `other` means Yantra's URL policy refused reads on that host; `blocked` names the robots, rate-limit, or blocklist refusal.                |

A read answered from an earlier failure adds no second notice, and a challenge page is reported only by the challenge rows above. When the breaker refused later searches, the `SEARCH_BLOCKED` notice says so, for example `3 of 3 web searches failed: the provider served an anti-bot challenge; 2 later searches were not attempted after the provider's challenge (SEARCH_BLOCKED).` Searches the breaker refused are counted that way; any other `web_search` call refused before the provider was asked, or one that was aborted or denied, is not counted as an attempted search. At most 10 runtime notices are attached: past that, the first nine are kept and a final `other` notice with source `runtime` reads `N more run notices are summarized in report.md under Run Health.` `metadata.search_provider` names the distinct providers the run searched through, joined by `, `, and stays `null` when no search ran. The same record produces the report's Run Health section and `run-health.json`; see [Run Health](diagnostics-and-audit.md#run-health).

### Exit codes and failures

|  Exit | Meaning for `do`                                                                                                                                                                         |
| ----: | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
|   `0` | A validated Brief or templated report was published.                                                                                                                                     |
|   `1` | Invalid command input, option, host, template/no-model combination, or user-input marker. Explicit `--no-llm` and `LLM_PROVIDER=none` also take this path because `do` requires a model. |
|   `2` | The started task failed, exhausted a fatal budget, or could not produce a valid publication.                                                                                             |
|   `3` | Model credentials were unavailable during the command's offline preflight. No agent session is opened.                                                                                   |
|   `4` | Yantra needs a user handoff, for example a missing required location, CAPTCHA, bot wall, ethics refusal, or denied protected action.                                                     |
| `130` | The run was interrupted with Ctrl+C.                                                                                                                                                     |

Startup and runtime errors use stable codes such as `AGENT_MODEL_NOT_FOUND`, `AGENT_AUTH_UNAVAILABLE`, `AGENT_PROVIDER_UNAVAILABLE`, `AGENT_SESSION_START_FAILED`, `AGENT_TOOL_FAILED`, `AGENT_BUDGET_EXHAUSTED`, and `AGENT_COMPLETION_MISSING`. Messages are sanitized and name a corrective action without exposing credentials. See [Errors and exit codes](diagnostics-and-audit.md#errors-and-exit-codes).

## Configuration and Permissions

Model settings resolve in this order: explicit flag, `YANTRA_AGENT_*` environment variable, `profile.yaml` `agent.*` preference, then the pinned default. Current defaults are Anthropic with `claude-haiku-4-5`, a 15-minute hard deadline, a 2,000,000-token ceiling, three-minute tool and confirmation timeouts, and a `--tool-retries` value of 3 (the run stops when one tool fails with the same error four times without succeeding in between). At 80% of the run duration, non-terminal exploration stops so the agent can publish gathered evidence.

Additional enforced defaults bound one model-visible tool result to 24 KB, cumulative model-visible tool output to 512 KB, browser navigations to 30, and distinct outbound hosts to 20. Publication remains available after the soft wind-down or cumulative-byte limit, but not after the hard deadline. Tool-call counts are recorded for audit and are not a cap.

Model credentials can come from Yantra-managed Pi auth, `--auth-secret`/`YANTRA_AGENT_AUTH_SECRET` as an OS-keychain reference, a supported provider environment variable, or custom-model configuration. Credential values are never written to prompts, logs, or run artifacts. `do` does not silently fall back when model auth is unavailable; use `yantra doctor` to inspect the effective model, credential source, and budgets without contacting a provider, or `yantra doctor --agent-smoke` for a live check.

All tools pass through input validation, placeholder resolution, budgets and timeouts, outbound host/ethics/scope policy, confirmation when required, sanitization, output bounding, and audit recording. The model cannot bypass or reorder those checks. Built-in provider shell, filesystem, edit, and unrestricted network tools are disabled.

Outbound URLs are length-capped, HTTPS-only by default, scanned for credential-shaped substrings, and charged against navigation and host budgets. Browser navigation and `web_fetch` also require provenance: the URL or its route shape must come from the user's goal, an explicit `--allow-host`, a search/fetch result, a URL a page read offered, a prior page action or redirect, or an intercepted popup. Query values may change on an attested route; the agent may not invent new paths, parameter names, or identifiers. `--allow-host example.com` restricts policy to that host and its subdomains and grants that user-named host for provenance.

Search, fetch, and navigation honor robots rules, the blocklist, rate limits, and site refusals. Yantra reports CAPTCHAs, bot walls, paywalls, and ethics blocks rather than evading them. Page and search content is always treated as untrusted data, not as instructions.

Protected clicks such as buy, pay, purchase, book, order, submit, or confirm actions require consent. Filling a host-bound website secret also requires consent. An attended TTY run displays the action, host, and consequence and defaults to deny; the wait is bounded by `--confirm-timeout` and the remaining run duration. `--json`, piped/non-TTY execution, timeout, or absence of a consent surface fails closed. Decisions and tool calls retain confirmation linkage in the run audit.

Website secrets must carry trusted host metadata before `browser_fill_element` will resolve them. The plaintext exists only during that fill and is never returned to the model or audit output. For one-off values, explicit input markers offer run-scoped separation; for durable credentials, use keychain-backed secret references.

Personalization includes only approved, sanitized preferences. Date, timezone, and locale are always supplied as run facts; user location is supplied only when `context.location` is enabled and `locale.city`/`locale.region` provides a value. See [Ambient run facts and location grants](profiles-and-history.md#states-ambient-run-facts-without-guessing-location).

## Limitations

- `do` requires a configured model. It has no deterministic `--no-llm` execution path; use `yantra ask --no-llm`, `yantra research --no-llm`, or a saved `yantra run` workflow when deterministic behavior is required.
- Yantra is limited to browser automation and public-web research. It exposes no general desktop control, arbitrary shell, unrestricted filesystem, arbitrary JavaScript, or user-supplied code execution.
- Browser profiles are fresh and ephemeral. Logged-in state does not persist between runs, and persistent browser profiles are unsupported. Only one run page is active; same-site result tabs may replace it, while cross-site popups require an explicit, policy-checked navigation.
- Browser control depends on observable, accessible page semantics. Hidden, disabled, ambiguous, stale, or unusually implemented controls may return typed failures. The fill engine retries boundedly and never claims success without verifying the committed value.
- Multi-field form fill accepts one through ten non-secret fields and does not submit. Stored secrets must be filled individually with host binding and confirmation. Literal credential-shaped fill values are refused.
- `web_fetch` accepts readable text pages, not PDFs, images, binaries, paywall bypasses, or arbitrary downloads. JavaScript-heavy pages, bot defenses, CAPTCHAs, robots rules, and rate limits can reduce evidence or require handoff.
- After the provider's first anti-bot challenge or rate-limit refusal, search stays closed for the rest of the run. Yantra does not fall back to another provider, so a run on a scraped provider may finish with only the evidence it gathered before then. `yantra doctor` warns when a run would use a scraped provider.
- A page is fetched at most once per run, so `web_fetch` does not pick up changes a page makes during the run; `browser_extract` reads the live page.
- One read shows at most 25 records, 40 links, 10 tables, 60 fields, and 25 structured entities. No tool lists the rest of a page; more records are reachable only through a `pagination` link the page offers. Filters that only a script applies, "load more" buttons, and checkbox filters inside forms are not offered as links.
- A link the sanitizer would alter, such as one whose path contains a masked value, is withheld as `url: null` rather than offered in a changed form, so it cannot be followed.
- Shape detection is structural and generic. A page whose repeated items do not share a common structure, or whose attributes are not written as label/value pairs, may read as an article or an index page.
- Challenge detection relies on a documented list of generic widget markers and phrases. A human-verification page that carries none of them is not recognized as one.
- Evidence-ledger sources distinguish cited pages from pages also consulted. The anchoring check can flag unsupported cited values but does not prove that every model-authored statement is entailed, correct, or current. Inspect consequential claims, conditions, and notices against the linked sources.
- Report-template runs require a valid model-authored slot payload. The runtime cannot safely assemble a missing templated report from free-form draft prose, so an invalid or missing template publication remains a failure.
- `--save-as` promotes only the successful browser trace. It cannot preserve transient login state or run-scoped marked values, and later replay may still need workflow parameters, stored website secrets, confirmation, and a compatible page structure.

For the detailed runtime and safety contracts, see [Agentic task architecture](../architecture.md#agentic-task) and [browser, URL, and web safety](safety-and-privacy.md#browser-url-and-web-safety).
